findings.reason: This edit makes `validateTags` depend on a UID, but the existing calls in `src/topics/create.js` and `src/posts/edit.js` still pass only tags and category. Consequently, ordinary topic creation and editing evaluate reserved tags with an undefined UID: regular users are rejected, but privileged users are rejected too, violating the required privilege distinction. `validateTag` also normalizes the submitted tag but not entries in `systemTags`, allowing a differently cased configured tag to evade its check.

The new `Topics.addTags` call to `validateTags(req.body.tags, cid, req.user.uid)` applies the category's minimum-tag count to only the tags in this addition request. A valid request adding one tag to an existing topic in a category requiring two tags is now rejected, even if the topic already has enough tags.

The new `isTagAllowed` check treats `systemTags` as empty unless it is already an array. No array default was added for `systemTags`; `meta/configs.js` only JSON-serializes and deserializes array settings that have array defaults. A reserved list saved through the normal config path can therefore reload as a string, making this socket check allow a reserved tag for a regular user.
